title: The combination of bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation reveals that Licoisoflavone A regulates the inflammatory response of endothelial cells in venous thromboembolism through KDM5B.
authors: Chen, BoYa; Lyu, Pin; Zhao, Bowen; Chang, Zhenghui; Gu, Zhichun; Huo, Mengqi; Sun, Jun
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过转录组和孟德尔随机化鉴定KDM5B为VTE风险基因，并用分子对接验证黄酮类化合物与其结合，但核心是炎症调控而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, with limited options to prevent recurrence and vascular injury. This study identifies KDM5B as a novel VTE risk gene and therapeutic target through integrated transcriptomics and Mendelian randomization. We further demonstrate that Licoisoflavone A, a flavonoid from Glycyrrhiza glabra, binds stably to KDM5B and attenuates endothelial inflammation. In IL-1beta-stimulated endothelial cells, Licoisoflavone A downregulated KDM5B and VCAM-1, suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines, and inhibited TNF/NF-kappaB signaling. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized anti-thrombotic mechanism of Licoisoflavone A and support its potential as a candidate therapy for VTE.
abstract_zh: 静脉血栓栓塞症（VTE）是发病率和死亡率的主要原因，目前预防复发和血管损伤的选项有限。本研究通过整合转录组学和孟德尔随机化，将KDM5B识别为新的VTE风险基因和治疗靶点。我们进一步证明，来自光果甘草（Glycyrrhiza glabra）的黄酮类化合物Licoisoflavone A能稳定结合KDM5B并减轻内皮炎症。在IL-1β刺激的内皮细胞中，Licoisoflavone A下调KDM5B和VCAM-1，抑制促炎细胞因子，并阻断TNF/NF-κB信号通路。这些发现揭示了Licoisoflavone A一种先前未被识别的抗血栓机制，并支持其作为VTE候选治疗药物的潜力。
